Incorporating SLOOS evidence tilts the tone slightly more negative than your initial read. The Q3 2020 SLOOS indicates:
- Banks tightened standards broadly for C&I and CRE loans, with softer demand—signaling headwinds for business credit.
- Mortgage demand strengthened mainly in safer segments (GSE-eligible, QM non-jumbo) while subprime demand was weaker; forbearance and bank capital positions influenced lending practices.
These findings imply that, despite the Fed’s accommodative stance and asset purchases supporting market functioning, the bank-intermediated credit channel remained restrictive, reinforcing downside risks flagged in the FOMC statement and FSR. Robust demand in GSE-eligible mortgages tempers the negativity, so the adjustment is modest.
